site.account.data.download.note: Account page: button that downloads a file with everything the bridge keeps about the account.

site.account.data.hint.text: Download everything this bridge keeps about you: your details, how you sign in, your domains and their traffic counts. What <privacy>we keep, and why</privacy>.
site.account.data.hint.note: Account page: text above the Download my data button. The bridge is our relay service. <privacy> links to the privacy notice.

site.account.data.title.note: Account page: title of the box for downloading the account's data and deleting the account.

site.account.delete.button.note: Account page: red button that deletes the account, for good.

site.account.delete.failed.note: Account page: error when the account could not be deleted and the bridge gave no reason.

site.account.delete.hint.text: Deleting your account releases all your domains (each name stays reserved for you for 30 days, so no one can pose as your device to your friends) and removes your details, sign-ins and setup codes. Your devices keep working at home, at {address}, as if they had been set up without an account - with everything on them - but are no longer reachable from outside nor by your friends. This can't be undone.
site.account.delete.hint.note: Account page: what deleting the account does, above the deletion fields. <b> marks the opening words in bold. {address} is the device's address on the home network (http://otc.local:8080), in code style (<code>).

site.account.delete.password_label.note: Account page, account deletion: label of the field where the account's password is typed to delete it.

site.account.delete.provider_hint.text: You sign in with Google or Apple: sign in again just before deleting (within 15 minutes).
site.account.delete.provider_hint.note: Account page, account deletion: shown instead of the password field to an account without a password (made with Google or Apple).

site.account.delete.type_error.note: Account page, account deletion: error when Delete my account is pressed without typing the word. {word} is the word to type, site.account.delete.word.

site.account.delete.type_label.note: Account page, account deletion: label of the field where a word is typed to confirm. {word} is the word to type (site.account.delete.word), in bold (<b>).

site.account.delete.word.note: Account page, account deletion: the word typed to confirm deleting the account, shown in bold in site.account.delete.type_label and in site.account.delete.type_error. One short lowercase word that is easy to type on a phone (the check ignores capitals and spaces around it). It is only compared on the page: the bridge always receives the English "delete", and typing "delete" is accepted too.

site.account.deleted.home.note: Account page: link to the site's home page, shown once the account was deleted.

site.account.deleted.lead.text: Your devices go on working at home, at {address}.
site.account.deleted.lead.note: Account page: paragraph under Your account is deleted, for an account that had no domains. {address} is the device's address on the home network (http://otc.local:8080), in code style (<code>).

site.account.deleted.lead_released.text: Released: {domains}. Your devices go on working at home, at {address}.
site.account.deleted.lead_released.note: Account page: paragraph under Your account is deleted. {domains} is the list of the domains released (name.off-the.cloud), separated by commas; {address} is the device's address on the home network (http://otc.local:8080), in code style (<code>).

site.account.deleted.title.note: Account page: heading shown once the account was deleted.

site.account.domains.connected.note: Account page, list of domains: state of a domain whose device is connected to the bridge right now (under the domain, and as the tooltip of the green dot). Lower case: it may be followed by " · disabled" and " · since <date>".

site.account.domains.disabled.note: Account page, list of domains: shown after connected or not connected, after a middle dot, when the domain was disabled by us. Lower case.

site.account.domains.empty.text: No domains yet. Set up a device with a setup code, or register a name for a manual install.
site.account.domains.empty.note: Account page: shown in place of the list of domains while the account has none.

site.account.domains.identity_confirm.text: Give {domain} a new identity? The device using it now will be locked out of the bridge until it is set up with the new one.
site.account.domains.identity_confirm.note: Account page: the browser's confirmation dialog after New identity. {domain} is the device's address (name.off-the.cloud). The identity is the device's secret credentials for the bridge.

site.account.domains.identity_failed.note: Account page, list of domains: error when a new identity could not be made and the bridge gave no reason.

site.account.domains.new_identity.note: Account page, list of domains: small button that gives the domain new secret credentials (a confirmation follows).

site.account.domains.not_connected.note: Account page, list of domains: state of a domain whose device is not connected to the bridge (under the domain, and as the tooltip of the red dot). Lower case, like connected.

site.account.domains.release.note: Account page, list of domains: small red button that gives the domain up (a confirmation follows).

site.account.domains.release_confirm.text: Release {domain}? Its device goes on working at home only ({address}), and the name stays reserved for you for 30 days.
site.account.domains.release_confirm.note: Account page: the browser's confirmation dialog after Release. {domain} is the device's address (name.off-the.cloud); {address} is the device's address on the home network (http://otc.local:8080).

site.account.domains.release_failed.note: Account page, list of domains: error when the domain could not be released and the bridge gave no reason.

site.account.domains.since.note: Account page, list of domains: the last item of a domain's state line, after a middle dot. {date} is the day the domain was registered, already written in the page's language. Lower case.

site.account.domains.title.note: Account page: title of the list of the account's domains (the devices' addresses, name.off-the.cloud).

site.account.error.confirm_required.note: Account page: error (lower case, like the bridge's) when a request to delete the account came without its confirmation. {body} is the confirmation the request must carry, written as data: {"confirm": "delete"}. The page always sends it, so people should not see this.

site.account.error.recent_signin_require.text: sign in again (with Google or Apple), then try again within 15 minutes
site.account.error.recent_signin_require.note: Account page: error (lower case, like the bridge's) when adding a password or deleting the account needs a sign-in with Google or Apple from the last 15 minutes.

site.account.field.country.note: Account page: label of the list where the person picks the country they live in (sign-up and the account's details).

site.account.field.country_choose.note: Account page: first entry of the country list, shown while no country is picked.

site.account.field.email.note: Account page: label of an email address field (sign-in, sign-up, and the account's details, where it can't be changed).

site.account.field.name.note: Account page: label of the first-name field (sign-up and the account's details).

site.account.field.surname.note: Account page: label of the surname field (sign-up and the account's details).

site.account.footer.privacy.note: Account page: link at the bottom of the page to the privacy notice (which stays in English).

site.account.forgot.email_label.note: Account page, sign-in box: label of the field for the email address a password-reset link is sent to.

site.account.forgot.open.note: Account page, sign-in box: link that opens the field for asking a password-reset email.

site.account.forgot.send.note: Account page, sign-in box: button that asks for a password-reset email.

site.account.forgot.sent.text: If there is an account for that email, a link to reset its password is on its way. It works for an hour.
site.account.forgot.sent.note: Account page, sign-in box: message after asking for a password-reset email. It must not say whether the account exists: the same answer is given for any address.

site.account.header.sign_out.note: Account page: small button at the top right, next to the signed-in email address.

site.account.home.hello.note: Account page: main heading once signed in. {name} is the account holder's first name.

site.account.home.summary.text:
{registered} of {max} domains registered · free until {date} ·
your details
site.account.home.summary.note: Account page: line under the main heading once signed in, three parts separated by a middle dot. {registered} is how many domains the account has, {max} how many it may have (5); {date} is when the free period ends, a date already written in the page's language, in bold (<b>); <details> links to the form for changing the account's name and country.

site.account.identity.yours.text: {domain} is yours. Copy this now - it is not shown again:
site.account.identity.yours.note: Account page: line above the new device identity (two lines of secret values) after registering a name or asking for a new identity. {domain} is the device's address (name.off-the.cloud), in bold (<b>). The values are shown only this once.

site.account.loading.note: Account page: shown for a moment while the page loads the account.

site.account.manual.failed.note: Account page: error when the device name could not be registered and the bridge gave no reason.

site.account.manual.hint.text: For a device installed with the install script rather than the image: register its name here and put the identity you get into {path} before running the script (it is shown once).
site.account.manual.hint.note: Account page: text of the box for registering a name by hand. The image is the system image written to the microSD card; the identity is the device's secret credentials for the bridge, shown only once. {path} is a file's path on the device (/etc/otc/otc-install.env), in code style (<code>).

site.account.manual.name_label.note: Account page, box for registering a name by hand: label of the field for the device's name (its address will be name.off-the.cloud), not a person's name.

site.account.manual.name_placeholder.note: Account page: grey example inside the empty device-name field, which is followed by .off-the.cloud. "casa" is an example name (lower-case letters, digits and hyphens only); another short example word is fine.

site.account.manual.register.note: Account page: button that registers the device name typed in the field.

site.account.manual.title.note: Account page: title of the box for registering a device's name by hand, for a device installed with the install script.

site.account.meta.description.text: Sign in to see the domains registered to your Off The Cloud account, release them, replace a lost device, and get a setup code for a new one.
site.account.meta.description.note: Account page: the description search engines show under the page's title. A domain is an address of the form name.off-the.cloud; a setup code links a new device to the account.

site.account.meta.title.note: Account page (off-the.cloud/account): the browser tab's title and the page's title in search results.

site.account.password.add.note: Account page, password box: the save button for an account that has no password yet (made with Google or Apple).

site.account.password.change.note: Account page, password box: button that saves the new password.

site.account.password.current_label.note: Account page, password box: label of the field for the password in use now.

site.account.password.mismatch.note: Account page: error under the new-password fields when the two passwords typed differ.

site.account.password.new_label.note: Account page: label of the new-password field (resetting a forgotten password, changing or adding one). <small> is the hint in smaller grey text after the label. {min_chars} is the shortest password allowed (8).

site.account.password.provider_hint.text: You sign in with Google or Apple. You can add a password within 15 minutes of signing in that way.
site.account.password.provider_hint.note: Account page, password box: shown instead of the current-password field to an account without a password (made with Google or Apple).

site.account.password.repeat_label.note: Account page: label of the field where the new password is typed a second time.

site.account.password.save_failed.note: Account page, password box: error when the password could not be saved and the bridge gave no reason.

site.account.password.saved.text: Password saved. Other sessions are signed out.
site.account.password.saved.note: Account page: green message at the top of the page after the password was changed.

site.account.password.sign_out_all.note: Account page, password box: small red button that ends every session of the account (a confirmation follows).

site.account.password.sign_out_all_confi.text: Sign out of your account on every browser and device, this one included?
site.account.password.sign_out_all_confi.note: Account page: the browser's confirmation dialog after Sign out everywhere.

site.account.password.signs_out.text: Changing the password signs you out everywhere else. Left signed in on a computer you don't use any more?
site.account.password.signs_out.note: Account page, password box: hint above the Sign out everywhere button.

site.account.password.title.note: Account page: title of the box for changing the password and signing out of other browsers.

site.account.profile.back.note: Account page, the account's details: button that returns to the account without saving.

site.account.profile.lead_edit.text: Update the details on your account.
site.account.profile.lead_edit.note: Account page: paragraph under the heading Your details.

site.account.profile.lead_new.text: We need a name and your country of residence to finish creating the account.
site.account.profile.lead_new.note: Account page: paragraph under the heading Almost there.

site.account.profile.save.note: Account page, the account's details: button that saves them.

site.account.profile.save_continue.note: Account page, the account's details: the save button when the person came from setting up a device and goes back to it afterwards.

site.account.profile.save_failed.note: Account page, the account's details: error when they could not be saved and the bridge gave no reason.

site.account.profile.title_edit.note: Account page: heading of the form for changing the account's name and country.

site.account.profile.title_new.note: Account page: heading of the form asking a new account (made with Google or Apple) for its name and country before it is complete.

site.account.reset.card_title.note: Account page, password reset: title of the box holding the new-password fields.

site.account.reset.done.text: Your new password is set, and you are signed in.
site.account.reset.done.note: Account page: green message at the top of the page after a password reset succeeded.

site.account.reset.failed.note: Account page, password reset: error when the new password could not be saved and the bridge gave no reason. "it" is the new password.

site.account.reset.set.note: Account page, password reset: button that saves the new password.

site.account.reset.signs_out.text: Setting it signs your account out everywhere else.
site.account.reset.signs_out.note: Account page, password reset: hint under the button. Saving the new password ends the account's sessions in every other browser and app.

site.account.reset.title.note: Account page: heading of the page a password-reset email's link opens.

site.account.send_failed.text: Could not send it right now
site.account.send_failed.note: Account page: error when an email (a password-reset link, or the confirmation link again) could not be sent and the bridge gave no reason.

site.account.setup.expires.note: Account page, setup-code box: line under the code just made. {minutes} is how long the code stays valid (15).

site.account.setup.failed.note: Account page, setup-code box: error when no setup code could be made and the bridge gave no reason.

site.account.setup.get.note: Account page: button that shows a new setup code.

site.account.setup.hint.text: Flash the image, power the device on and set it up from the iOS or Android app (Set up a new device, over Bluetooth). At the account step choose I have a setup code and type this code - it links the new device's name to this account. Good for 15 minutes.
site.account.setup.hint.note: Account page: text of the setup-code box. The image is the system image written to the microSD card. "Set up a new device" and "I have a setup code" (in bold, <b>) are the words the apps and the setup page show: use their translations. The code expires after 15 minutes.

site.account.setup.lost.text: Lost a device? Set up its replacement the same way and give it the same name: the name moves to the new device and the old one is locked out.
site.account.setup.lost.note: Account page: hint at the bottom of the setup-code box. The name is the device's address (name.off-the.cloud), in bold (<b>); the old device can no longer use it.

site.account.setup.title.note: Account page: title of the box that gives a setup code.

site.account.signed_out.lead.text: One account holds the domains of your devices: sign in here to see them, replace a lost device, or get a code for setting up a new one.
site.account.signed_out.lead.note: Account page: paragraph under the main heading while nobody is signed in. A domain is a device's address (name.off-the.cloud).

site.account.signed_out.title.note: Account page: main heading while nobody is signed in.

site.account.signin.button.note: Account page, sign-in box: the button that signs in.

site.account.signin.continue_with.note: Account page: button that signs in or creates the account through another company's account. {provider} is Google or Apple.

site.account.signin.failed.note: Account page, sign-in box: error when signing in failed and the bridge gave no reason.

site.account.signin.password_label.note: Account page, sign-in box: label of the password field.

site.account.signin.title.note: Account page: title of the sign-in box.

site.account.signin_error.cancelled.note: Account page: error at the top of the page (lower case) when a sign-in with Google or Apple was stopped before it finished.

site.account.signin_error.expired.text: that sign-in has expired, please try again
site.account.signin_error.expired.note: Account page: error at the top of the page (lower case) when a sign-in with Google or Apple took too long or was started in another browser.

site.account.signin_error.failed.text: the sign-in could not be completed
site.account.signin_error.failed.note: Account page: error at the top of the page (lower case) when a sign-in with Google or Apple failed, for any other reason.

site.account.signin_error.no_email.text: the sign-in did not include an email address
site.account.signin_error.no_email.note: Account page: error at the top of the page (lower case) when Google or Apple did not share an email address they confirmed.

site.account.signup.button.note: Account page, sign-up box: the button that creates the account.

site.account.signup.failed.note: Account page, sign-up box: error when the account could not be created and the bridge gave no reason.

site.account.signup.password_label.note: Account page, sign-up box: label of the password field. <small> is the hint in smaller grey text after the label. {min_chars} is the shortest password allowed (8).

site.account.signup.providers.text: Or create it with a sign-in provider (you accept the terms on the next page):
site.account.signup.providers.note: Account page, sign-up box: line above the Continue with Google and Continue with Apple buttons. "it" is the account; the terms are the terms of use, accepted on the page that follows the provider's sign-in.

site.account.signup.title.note: Account page: title of the sign-up box.

site.account.terms.accept.text: I accept the <terms>terms of use</terms> and have read the <privacy>privacy notice</privacy>.
site.account.terms.accept.note: Account page: text of the checkbox that accepts the terms (sign-up, the account's details, and the box asking an existing account to accept new terms). <terms> links to the terms of use and <privacy> to the privacy notice, both in a new tab.

site.account.terms.accept_button.note: Account page: button that records the acceptance of the terms of use, under the checkbox.

site.account.terms.intro.text: Creating an account is only necessary to use our bridge: you will get up to {max_domains} domains like name.{host} to connect to your device and also connect with the devices of your friends and family. If you only want to use your device in your local network as a NAS or with Tailscale Funnel, you do not need an account.
site.account.terms.intro.note: Account page: first paragraph of the summary of the terms, shown at sign-up and at the bottom of the account. The bridge is our relay service that makes a device reachable from outside the home. {max_domains} is how many domains an account gets (5); name.{host} shows the form of a domain: name is a placeholder word in italics for the name the person chooses, {host} is the site's address (off-the.cloud).

site.account.terms.pricing.text: An account for up to {max_domains} domains is free for the first {free_years} years, and after this period will cost {price} euros + VAT a year (we will e-mail you before the period ends). If you need more domains, each extra one costs {extra_domain_eur} euros a year: please contact us at {contact}. An account unused for {inactive_months} months (no sign-in here, and no app or friend reaching your devices through the bridge) is removed and its domains released; we email you a month before. Read the full terms of use and the privacy notice.
site.account.terms.pricing.note: Account page: second paragraph of the summary of the terms (prices and removal of unused accounts), after the first. {max_domains} (5), {free_years} (2), {extra_domain_eur} (2) and {inactive_months} (6) are numbers; {price} is the yearly price, already written as a number of the page's language (9.99); {contact} is our email address, a link (<mail>). <terms> links to the terms of use and <privacy> to the privacy notice, both in a new tab.

site.account.terms.prompt.text: We have published <terms>terms of use</terms> for accounts and the bridge. Please read and accept them: until then this account can't register device names or give setup codes.
site.account.terms.prompt.note: Account page: text of the box asking an account to accept the terms. <terms> links to the terms of use, in a new tab. The bridge is our relay service; a device name is the device's address (name.off-the.cloud); a setup code links a new device to the account.

site.account.terms.prompt_title.note: Account page: title of the box asking an account to accept the terms of use (published after it was created, or changed since).

site.account.terms.save_failed.note: Account page: error when the acceptance of the terms could not be recorded and the bridge gave no reason.

site.account.terms.tick.text: Tick the box to accept them.
site.account.terms.tick.note: Account page: error when Accept is pressed without ticking the checkbox. "them" is the terms of use.

site.account.verify.done.text: Your email is confirmed. You can register your devices now.
site.account.verify.done.note: Account page: green message at the top of the page after the link of the confirmation email was opened.

site.account.verify.failed.note: Account page: error at the top of the page when the confirmation email's link could not be used and the bridge gave no reason.

site.account.verify.prompt.text: We sent a link to {email}. Open it to confirm the address is yours - until then this account can't register device names or give setup codes.
site.account.verify.prompt.note: Account page: text of the box shown until the email address is confirmed. {email} is the account's email address, in bold (<b>). A device name is the device's address (name.off-the.cloud); a setup code links a new device to the account.

site.account.verify.prompt_title.note: Account page: title of the box shown until the account's email address is confirmed.

site.account.verify.resend.note: Account page: button in the confirm-your-email box that sends the confirmation email again.

site.account.verify.resent.text: Sent - check your inbox (and the spam folder).
site.account.verify.resent.note: Account page: message under the Send the link again button once the email is on its way.
